extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, and researchers interested in social psychology and psychoanalysis
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of crowd (mob) psychology and related theories, summarizing origins, types of crowds, major theoretical perspectives (Le Bon, Freud, deindividuation, convergence, emergent-norm, social identity), and basic tenets and methods of psychoanalysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influences on crowd behavior: loss of responsibility and impression of universality
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd behavior is heavily influenced by the loss of responsibility of the individual and the impression of universality of behavior, both of which increase with the size of the crowd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dimension is presented as a central explanatory factor for how crowds behave and why individual accountability diminishes in larger gatherings; the text notes security implications and contemporary relevance (e.g., Occupy Movement, London Riots).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of crowds (active vs passive; aggressive/escapist/acquisitive/expressive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowds can be active (mobs) or passive (audiences). Active crowds are further divided into aggressive (violent, outwardly focused), escapist (panic situations), acquisitive (competing for limited resources, e.g., looting), and expressive (gatherings for active, often nonviolent purposes like concerts or religious revivals).
